title: Understanding Transition Probabilities
text:
Let ({X_n}_{n}) be a Markov chain.
The transition probability from state (i) to state (j) is defined as
\[
p(i,j)
=
P(X_{n+1}=j \mid X_n=i).
\]

title: Understanding Transition Probabilities
text:
Interpretation
The quantity (p(i,j)) represents the probability that the chain moves to state (j) at the next step, given that its current state is (i).

title: Understanding Transition Probabilities
text:
Two-step transition probabilities
To move from (i) to (j) in two steps, the chain may pass through any intermediate state (k). Therefore,
\[
p^{(2)}(i,j)
=
\sum_{k\in S}p(i,k)p(k,j).
\]
